items.title: Federal judge blocks the FCC from reviewing ABC’s licenses early
items.snippet: US District Judge Loren AliKhan has blocked the Federal Communications Commission from conducting an early review of ABC's broadcast licenses in a preliminary injunction, and rejected its efforts to dismiss ABC's First Amendment lawsuit. ABC has accused the FCC of violating its free speech rights and claims the agency "waged a retaliatory campaign" against the network over content it broadcast. In her ruling the judge noted that the network was "likely to succeed on their retaliation claim." Although Disney, ABC's parent company, wasn't set to renew its broadcast licenses until 2028, last April the FCC ordered the network to file for an ear … Read the full story at The Verge.

items.title: GTA VI developers vote against unionization
items.snippet: Workers at Grand Theft Auto VI developer Rockstar Games won't unionize, after the vote for a formal recognition agreement failed, with only 25 percent of votes in favor of unionization. The Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB) said that Rockstar workers in the union will continue organizing even without formal recognition. Voting ran from November 12th through 26th, covering the launch of GTA VI . If successful, the vote would have established a formal framework for collective negotiation with the studio over pay, overtime, bonuses, leave, and pensions, along with a right to consultation over future changes including AI implemen … Read the full story at The Verge.

items.title: Why GTA VI’s version of Florida feels so real
items.snippet: There are plenty of reasons why Grand Theft Auto VI is so popular : the 13 years of anticipation , the relatable lead characters and romantic storyline , the sheer level of depth . But another major factor is the sense of place. The GTA series is unmatched when it comes to re-creating the feeling of a bustling, real-world city, and GTA VI 's fictional rendition of Florida is the studio's most lifelike setting yet. It has functioning buses and trains, plentiful buildings you can go into and explore, residents you can chat with, and huge areas where you can interact with wildlife far away from the bright lights of the Miami-like Vice City. items.title: Kodak Launches Unique AirTag Rival With E-Ink Display
items.snippet: Kodak licensee Reto this week introduced the SlideTag, a $34.99 Find My-compatible item tracker with a color E Ink screen for displaying personal photos. The SlideTag's design draws on Kodak's Kodachrome slide mounts, placing a square display inside a retro frame with an attachment point for a keyring. items.title: Wispr Flow improves dictation accuracy with new Canto-2 speech-to-text model
items.snippet: Popular AI dictation app Wispr Flow is rolling out a new speech-to-text model for Mac, iPhone, and other platforms, promising fewer transcription errors and better recognition of names and technical terms. Here are the details. Wispr Flow this week launched Canto-2, its newest speech-to-text model, which the company says reduces transcription errors by 36% across 14 languages and by more than 15% in English compared to its predecessor, Canto-1. In practice, that means the average error rate dropped from 9.9% to 6.3% across the 14 languages, and from 3.2% to 2.7% in English, according to Wispr’s internal benchmarks. According to the company, teaching a model to recognize specific names and terms comes with a trade-off: the more it relies on that user-specific context, the more likely it is to insert those words even when they weren’t actually spoken. Wispr notes that Canto-2 strikes a better balance between context and accuracy, improving its ability to recognize user-specific terms without substantially increasing the frequency of incorrect substitutions: Canto-2 recovers hard names…

items.title: Apps appear to flout Apple’s rules on iPhone notification ads
items.snippet: Apple has set some rules meant to curb unwanted iPhone notification ads, but some apps appear to be ignoring them. iPhone users have reported promos with no opt-out and ads in Live Activities. Apple’s guidelines address both, but people say the practices continue. Apple’s App Store Review Guidelines allow apps to send promotional push notifications. But there’s a catch. Users have to explicitly opt in through consent language in the app, with developers providing a way to opt out. Live Activities face stricter limits: Apple tells developers “Don’t use a Live Activity to display ads or promotions” and also bars using Live Activities to send unsolicited messages. In a post on X, Joe Rossignol wrote that several apps on his iPhone in Canada sent him prompts with no way to opt out. He named Cineplex, McDonald’s and Wendy’s. items.title: Sandboxed AI models can break out of isolation by exploiting variations in GPU rounding

The researchers also found a watchdog missed all 354 attacks in a test, while vLLM’s fixes for the channels are not enabled by default. Source

items.title: How to improve AI agents over time with models, harnesses, and context
